//: How fighting and powers are played back (12 §7.3; 07 §16, 08 §12): a line for a blow that lands, misses or is stopped, for a stagger and a fall, and for a power used or refused, each worded for the reader. A blow that lands on someone flashes a thud where they are; one only heard leaves a marker. What a blow does to the body is the condition screen's to show.
Falling senseless, coming to and dying (06 §8.3): without these lines a player fought on against someone already down, or died without a word (play-testing 2, decision D-910).

A wound made, wherever the blow was stopped: a knife blocked on the forearm cuts the forearm, and without a line the character bled to death after blows that were all stopped (play-testing 2, decision D-910).

What is done with something held (`core`'s `making/actions.json`): eaten, drunk, bound on, rubbed on, put on a blade, read. Without a line a bandage put on in a fight left nothing to show it had been (play-testing 2, decision D-910).
log: {the(self)} {if event.interaction == 'core:eat' then verb(self, 'eat') + ' ' + the(target) else if event.interaction == 'core:drink' then verb(self, 'drink') + ' ' + the(target) else if event.interaction == 'core:apply_bandage' then verb(self, 'bind') + ' ' + their(self) + ' wounds' else if event.interaction == 'core:apply_salve' then verb(self, 'rub') + ' on a salve' else if event.interaction == 'core:coat_blade' then verb(self, 'coat') + ' a blade' else verb(self, 'read') + ' ' + the(target)}.

//: A mode of a power switched on or ended (08 §5.4): with no line a player cannot tell that a power held up by its reserve has run dry.

log: {if event.how == 'empty' then cap(the(self)) + ' ' + verb(self, 'run') + ' dry, and a power fails.' else if event.how == 'ended' then cap(the(self)) + ' ' + verb(self, 'let') + ' a power go.' else 'A power of ' + the(self) + ' fails.'}

//: Speech (15 §11): what a character the player plays hears said is written in the log, the line as it was worded for that character; what one of them says to someone else is written once, from the one it was said to, without the words, which were worded for the hearer. The party sees every hearing that has one of its own among its subjects, so `party()` tells whose hearing it was.
if: not is_null(event.text) and self in party()
not is_null(speaker) and not is_null(to) and to == self and speaker in party() and not (self in party())
